The daemonset process accumulated 8 gigabytes of unmanaged memory on each node over a 6-hour period without hitting its container memory limit. As host memory utilization crossed the 90% eviction threshold, the kubelet on each node asserted memory pressure conditions.

The kubelet instances initiated mass pod evictions, terminating over 300 stateless application pods based on quality of service classes. Because evicted pods were rescheduled onto surviving node hosts that were already experiencing memory pressure, the influx of rescheduled workloads triggered a cascading eviction storm that disabled entire microservice deployments. Critical cluster add-ons, including autoscalers and metric collectors, were repeatedly evicted.

The site reliability engineering team arrested the cascade by cordoning all affected node hosts and deleting the faulty security daemonset across the cluster. We then reconfigured kubelet eviction thresholds with higher system-reserved memory allocations of 6 gigabytes per host instead. We enforced strict container resource quotas and memory limits on all daemonset manifests deployed across production clusters.
